name: Face-Stealer
body:
This species of shapechangers capable of changing their appearance to look like any other humanoid of the same basic size and shape. Commonly known as “face-stealers,” they are more charitably called the “imitators.” Many other names have been used to describe them, including (confusingly) “changelings” and (inaccurately) “half-doppelgangers.” Among themselves, they are known as the ekweeja.

No one knows quite where the face-stealers come from, only that some of them—in some places, entire communities of them—have infiltrated certain humanoid societies.

They live as part of their adopted cultures, hiding their true identities from a world that fears and misunderstands them.

Physical

Few people ever see a face-stealer in their natural form. Indeed, some face-stealers won’t ever assume their natural forms and may never have seen another face-stealer in that vulnerable, incredibly intimate state.

A face-stealer’s true form is said to be devoid of color. Their skin is pale white or gray, although in some individuals it takes on a silvery sheen, and in others in becomes semi-translucent, allowing the pinkish shade of their internal organs to be seen through the delicate skin. The eyes are solid white or pink, while the translucent hair usually looks white but can refract all the colors of the rainbow if caught from the right angle.

Face-stealers are naturally bidirectional hermaphrodites. Likewise, most are fluid when it comes to their own gender identity.

Social

Unlike doppelgangers, many of whom infiltrates humanoid society due to nefarious motives, most face-stealers seem to just want to be left alone. Each has their own reasons for using their abilities to blend into a community. While they can make consummate spies and criminals, not all of them put their talents to use in such deliberate ways—many prefer instead to maintain a much lower profile and live a more or less mundane life.

Face-stealers are masters of secrets. They maintain networks of useful contacts, many of them other face-stealers, whom they can leverage to grease wheels and make deals.

The most skilled face-stealers may have dozens of different established identities that they can seamlessly step into as needed. Some close face-stealer allies have even been known to share these identities in order to better establish a presence in a community or pull off a long-con.

Above all, maintaining the illusion remains all-important for the face-stealer. Breaking character is always the last resort—and many face-stealers would rather die in-character than let it be known that they are, in fact, an imposter.

Alignment And Religion

Like humans, face-stealers have a wide range of alignments. Overall, they are neutral, and if they favor any alignment it is Chaotic. Although they have their own code of honor—which they value very strongly—many face-stealers value nothing more than their own autonomy. They see their shapeshifting gifts as the ultimate escape-clause, a way to slip away anonymously from any situation they cannot control so that they can start again.

Face-stealers have no gods of their own. They favor human gods, or the gods of whatever humanoid society they have infiltrated. Gods of deception, trickery, secrecy, and opportunity are all favored, but many face-stealers find it expedient to pay tribute to many different gods—perhaps even practicing wildly different faiths with each different identity they adopt.

Names

A face-stealer will adopt many different personas throughout their lives, each with their own name and individual identity. Like their true appearance, their true name is something they rarely share except among family and close friends. These given names are usually very simple, compared to the sometimes elaborate identities that they can create for themselves when disguised.

Examples of face-stealer given names include the following (choose or roll 1d20): 1 Anko, 2 Bozdi, 3 Drifka, 4 Fesh, 5 Fogrix, 6 Fumak, 7 Koldo, 8 Kindi, 9 Lev, 10 Pawa, 11 Riz, 12 Skraya, 13 Soratti, 14 Stax, 15 Tan, 16 Tenyo, 17 Uda, 18 Weejen, 19 Wix, 20 Yuz

Standard Species Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are quick and convincing, but delicate. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Dex, +2 Cha, –2 Con [standard]. (0)
Size As a Medium creature, you have no bonuses or penalties due to size. (0)
Type You are a Humanoid with the ekweeja and shapechanger subtypes. (0)
Speed Your base speed is 30 feet. (0)
Languages You begin play speaking Common. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any language except for secret languages. (1)
Alternate Species Traits
Gift of Tongues In addition to your physical mastery of disguise, you have developed superior skills for interacting with those you are using your disguise against. You gain a +1 species bonus on Bluff and Diplomacy checks, and you learn one additional language every time you put a rank in the Linguistics skill. (2)
Simulacrum (Ex)

You can spend 1 minute to physically alter your form to look like any Medium humanoid with two arms and two legs, as long as you have seen a similar creature before. You can attempt to either mimic a specific creature you have seen or appear as a creature of your own design of that chosen species. You gain a +10 bonus to Disguise checks to appear as that creature, and the DC of this Disguise check is not modified as a result of altering major features or being disguised as a different species of humanoid. You can remain in your altered form indefinitely. (4)

Stubborn Having learned to play many different identities makes you difficult for others to master. You gain a +2 species bonus on Will saving throws to resist spells and spell-like abilities of the enchantment (charm) and enchantment (compulsion) subschools. In addition, if you fail such a save, you receive another save 1 round later to prematurely end the effect (assuming the spell or spell-like ability has a duration greater than 1 round). This second save is made at the same DC as the first. If you have a similar ability from another source (such as a rogue’s slippery mind class feature), you can only use one of these abilities per round, but can try the other on the second round if the first reroll ability fails. (2)
Total: 9 RP (standard)
Alternate Species Traits
Cautious You are especially wary of being discovered, and have learned to read others’ motivations carefully. You gain a +2 species bonus on Sense Motive checks. This trait replaces gift of tongues.
Darkvision You come from a long line of face-stealers that have operated from the shadows, dwelling in underground tunnels and only coming out at night. You gain darkvision with a range of 60 feet. This trait replaces stubborn.
Defensive Form Your shapechanging abilities are for more than just imitation. You can noticeably thicken your skin, providing you with a +1 natural armor bonus to AC and electricity resistance 5. You can only use this ability while in your natural form, and do not gain any benefits from it while using your simulacrum species trait. This trait replaces stubborn.
Domineering Assuming other identities has educated you in personal power dynamics, and you always know how to pull the right strings to bully and cajole others. You gain a +2 species bonus on Intimidation checks. This trait replaces gift of tongues.
Feats
Fast Change

You are capable of assuming a new form much more rapidly than most.

Prerequisite(s): simulacrum species trait, character level 3rd.

Benefit(s): Instead of requiring 1 minute, you can use your simulacrum species trait as a ? full-round action.

Alternative Favored Class Bonuses
Alchemist Add +1 extract formula from the alchemist’s list to your formula book. This formula must be at least 1 level lower than the highest level of alchemist formula you can create.
Bard Add +1 to your total number of bardic performance rounds per day.
Cleric Select one domain power granted at 1st level that is normally usable a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Wisdom modifier. Add +1/2 to the number of uses per day of that domain power.
Druid Add +1 skill rank to your animal companion. If you ever replaces your companion, the new companion gains these bonus skill ranks.
Magus Add +1/4 to your arcane pool.
Oracle Add +1 spell known from the oracle spell list. This spell must be at least one spell level below the highest-level oracle spell you can cast.
Ranger Add +1 skill rank to your animal companion. If you ever replaces your companion, the new companion gains these bonus skill ranks.
Rogue Add a +1/2 bonus on Bluff checks to pass secret messages and Diplomacy checks to gather information.
Sorcerer Add +1 spell known from the sorcerer spell list. This spell must be at least one spell level below the highest-level sorcerer spell you can cast.
Summoner Add +1 skill rank to your eidolon.
Swashbuckler Increase the number of times per day you can use charmed life by +1/4.
Vigilante Gain +1/2 on the Disguise bonus provided by seamless guise.
Witch Add +1 skill rank to your familiar. If you ever replaces your familiar, the new familiar gains these bonus skill ranks.
Wizard When casting wizard illusion spells, add +1/3 to the effective caster level of the spell, but only to determine the spell’s duration.
